newsitem.title: UK: Euro veg oils little changed, hampered by currency.
newsitem.headline: Euro veg oils little changed, hampered by currency.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices closed little changed on Friday, with business hampered by the firm dollar.
Higher Chicago futures at the opening, on forecasts of dry weather over the weekend in the U.S. Midwest, had no impact on prices.
"Chicago has become a sideshow, everybody is watching currency," said another trader.
No significant price changes were reported in the palm oil sector despite the higher Malaysian market, boosted by short-covering and the weak ringgit.
The holiday in Malaysia on Thursday, coupled with the currency situation, kept the market very quiet, traders said.
A weaker ringgit should make palm oil more attractive on the export market, giving the flagging market a much-needed boost.
At the close of business Dutch soy oil was unchanged to 0.50 guilders up after Nov/Jan traded at 103.75 guilders per 100 kilos.
Rape oil finished 0.50 guilders up to unchanged in a tradeless market.
Crude palm oil ended the day mixed at $2.50 up to $2.50 down in a tradeless market, while products were $2.50 lower with no further business reported.
In thin trading coconut oil gained $12.50 to $10 on the day with two trades reported, but not confirmed.
Aug/Sep coconut was reported traded at $592.50 with the same price paid for Oct/Nov.
"It could have been a switch at even money, but we can't confirm that," said one trader.
Palmkernel oil closed $10 higher, with no business reported.
